title: Geometric fibres and degree-zero pullback for constructible adic coefficients
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $k$, and let $h:V\to T$ be a morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in it. Use the raw rationalized categories $D^b_c(W,E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] and the common-finite-stage category $D^b_c(W,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], for $W=V,T$. All integral objects and pullbacks use the derived-complete coefficient categories with their compatible etale-origin witnesses, rather than discrete non-torsion coefficients on the small etale site. At the stage $\Lambda=E$ use the bounded t-structure of [prop-weil-localized-tstructure] on $D^b_c(W,E)$, induced by the localization functor $Q$ from the integral t-structure of [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure]: its classes and its heart consist of the objects isomorphic in $D^b_c(W,E)$ to some $QL$ with $L$ in the corresponding integral class, and for an integral object $L$ the degree-$r$ cohomology object $(\tau^{\ge r}\tau^{\le r}QL)[r]$ is $Q$ applied to the ambient cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^r(L)$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], placed in degree zero. At $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ the classes $D^{\le0}$, $D^{\ge0}$ and the heart consist of the objects isomorphic to some pair $(L,M)$ with $M$ in the corresponding class of $D^b_c(W,L)$ at a finite stage $L$; they form a bounded t-structure [def-weil-t-structure] whose truncations and cohomology objects are computed at a common finite stage and commute with finite coefficient extension. In both cases write $\operatorname{Sh}_c(W,\Lambda)$ for the heart and $\mathcal H^r$ for these cohomology objects. Membership in a class is invariant under isomorphism; in particular an integral object whose ambient cohomology is $\varpi$-power torsion outside degree zero lies in the rational heart.

The completed derived pullback $Lh^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], rationalized and passed to common finite stages, is an exact triangulated functor $D^b_c(T,\Lambda)\to D^b_c(V,\Lambda)$ and takes objects of $\operatorname{Sh}_c(T,\Lambda)$ to objects of $\operatorname{Sh}_c(V,\Lambda)$. Write $h^*\mathcal F$ for this degree-zero object when $\mathcal F$ lies in the heart.

For a geometric point $\bar v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V$ [def-weil-geometric-point], with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, put $\bar t=h\bar v$. Geometric coefficient fibres on the constructible hearts are exact and jointly conservative, and there is a natural isomorphism
$$ (h^*\mathcal F)_{\bar v}\cong\mathcal F_{\bar t}.$$
These are the adic geometric fibres: on a lisse integral stratum take the inverse limit of the finite-level etale fibres, then invert the uniformizer, and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ extend the resulting finite-stage $E$-vector space to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, as in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. They are independent, up to isomorphism, of the geometric point chosen over a fixed underlying point. The comparisons are natural in $\mathcal F$ and commute with finite coefficient extension.

Every sheaf in these hearts is lisse of finite rank on a finite locally closed stratification, with locally constant fibre ranks on each stratum. In particular its nonzero-geometric-fibre locus is a constructible subset [def-weil-constructible-subset] of $W$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2, Definition 6.8.3, Proposition 6.8.4, Definition 6.8.6, Lemma 6.8.7, Definitions 6.8.8 and 6.8.10, Proposition 6.8.11, Proposition 6.8.14, and Remark 6.8.15; constructible-heart and pullback consequences, with rationalization and common finite stages as specified in the statement

proof.text: The schemes $V,T$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to their structure maps to the one-point Noetherian scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$. They are finite-dimensional by [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound], whose bound on the sole fibre of either structure map is a bound on the scheme. The assumed unit $\ell\in k$ remains a unit in every local ring. Thus [prop-weil-pbc-integral-tstructure] and [prop-weil-localized-tstructure] apply, giving the integral and rational t-structures and the rational heart exactly as stated. Composing the two truncation comparisons of the latter theorem with the shift identifies the rational degree-$r$ cohomology of $QL$ with $Q\mathcal H^r(L)$, since the integral truncations are the ambient ones. These are isomorphism-closed classes; no assertion about the vanishing of the cohomology of every integral representative is made. If the finitely many nonzero ambient cohomology sheaves outside degree zero are killed by powers of $\varpi$, their images under $Q$ are zero: their identities become zero in the localized Hom groups of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. The localized cohomology formula and bounded truncation triangles then put $QL$ in the rational heart, as asserted.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3) and Proposition 6.8.14(2); integral and localized standard t-structures

proof.text: Use [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization] on each $W=V,T$. Write $B_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ and $E_W=B_W[1/\varpi]$. Its equivalence $J_W$ identifies the rational heart with the constructible continuous $E_W$-module sheaves. The coefficient sheaves are the continuous ones in [det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure], whose kernels and cokernels of constructible sheaf maps are constructible and whose inclusion in all module sheaves is exact. Thus exactness in this heart is precisely ordinary sheaf exactness in this model. This comparison uses completed coefficient sheaves; it never replaces $E_W$ by the discrete constant sheaf of $E$.

For $E\subset L$, [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies integral scalar extension with ordinary derived tensor by a finite free completed coefficient module. After choosing a basis only to check exactness, the underlying tensor functor is a finite direct sum and hence is exact. By [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] it preserves the cohomological halves. The integral constructible restriction and its exact rationalization are the functors of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], which applies under Step 1's general Noetherian finite-dimensional hypotheses. Since rational halves are isomorphism closures of integral halves, rational scalar extension is t-exact. The comparison theorem [lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison] gives its natural truncation comparisons. Its identity, composition and natural-transformation clauses make them compatible with the scalar associators and their unit and pentagon equations of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Cohomology, the indicated composite of truncations and a shift, has the same compatibility.

source.place: Propositions 6.8.11 and 6.8.14, finite extension of coefficient fields

proof.text: For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, descend each of the two truncation functors and its maps by [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent], using Step 3's scalar comparisons. The source pair category and its distinguished triangles are exactly [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Its scalar diagram is the one with associators in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], so the descent hypotheses hold. The formula sends $(E,K)$ to $(E,\tau_E K)$ and a common-stage arrow to its truncation conjugated by those comparisons. The theorem supplies independence of representatives, functoriality and descent of the truncation maps and their equations. Distinguished truncation triangles are represented by the finite-stage triangles.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and the prescribed common-finite-stage category; functorial descent of truncations

proof.text: These are the asserted bounded t-structure classes. Indeed shifting a representative proves the shift inclusions in [def-weil-t-structure]. For objects in degrees $\le0$ and $\ge1$, pass to a common coefficient field. Every further extension preserves these bounds by Step 3, so every Hom group in the directed system is zero by finite-stage orthogonality. Its colimit is the common-stage Hom group by [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], hence zero. Step 4 supplies the truncation triangle with its required end bounds. Each object already has two finite bounds at its field of definition. This proves the three axioms and boundedness. Their intersection is the isomorphism closure of finite-stage heart objects: for an object in the intersection its finite-stage nonzero-degree cohomologies become zero at a single further stage (there are only finitely many degrees); at that stage it is isomorphic to its degree-zero cohomology. Here being zero in the filtered Hom colimit means the identity becomes zero at a further stage. This also proves the stated description of the heart.

source.place: Common-stage t-structure axioms and boundedness, written out from the finite-stage structures

proof.text: The completed integral pullback preserves shifts and distinguished triangles by [lem-cbc-completed-pullback-triangles]. By [lem-a1-integral-pullback-completed-comparison] and [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible](1), it preserves the integral constructible categories, including the finite reduction witnesses. Its $A$-linear action therefore extends to an exact functor on raw rationalizations by [lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization]. The comparison with finite coefficient extension is [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], transported through the same completed-pullback comparison and extended on fractions by that localization lemma. Its unit and tower equations persist. Thus [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] gives the exact triangulated common-stage pullback as well. This proves the exact triangulated functor clause at both field stages, before proving preservation of the hearts.

source.place: Lemmas 6.5.9 and 6.8.2, Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; exactness and scalar-compatible completed pullback

proof.text: Let $\mathcal F$ be in the $E$-heart, represented under $J_T$ by a constructible $E_T$-module $F$. Choose a finite locally closed stratification where $F$ is lisse. On each stratum choose a pro-etale cover trivializing $F$ as $E^r$ with its continuous coefficient sheaf. Pull these strata and covers back to $V$: [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification] gives a finite locally closed stratification, constructible since $V$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-constructible-subset], and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] gives the base-changed covering families. By the composition and restriction comparisons of [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], the restriction of the actual pullback to each such chart is derived module pullback of the finite free model. A finite free module placed in degree zero is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]; its derived pullback is therefore the same finite free target module in degree zero, by $b'\otimes e_j\mapsto b'e_j$. Exact restriction commutes with cohomology, and [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-stratum-detection] now kills every other cohomology sheaf. Hence $Lh^*\mathcal F$ lies in the target heart. This uses fibre-product strata, including empty ones, and needs no flatness assertion about $h^{-1}E_T\to E_V$.

source.place: Definitions 6.8.6 and 6.8.8, Remark 6.8.15; local finite-free calculation of degree-zero pullback

proof.text: A bounded object is built from its finitely many cohomology objects by truncation triangles. Since pullback is triangulated and preserves the heart by Step 7, induction through these triangles preserves its cohomological interval: each $\mathcal H^j(K)[-j]$ stays in degree $j$, and the two halves are extension-closed by [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](2),(5). Thus pullback is t-exact at $E$. The common-stage object formula of [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] and the isomorphism-closed description in Step 5 show that it preserves both halves and the heart at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. A short exact heart sequence is a distinguished triangle by [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles](4); its image is a distinguished triangle of heart objects and hence is short exact. We may therefore write its restriction as $h^*$.

source.place: Bounded truncation devissage after Remark 6.8.15; heart exactness

proof.text: Define the geometric fibre of $F$ using its lisse stratum. Choose an affine etale integral-model chart at the point by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-affine-etale-lattice], applied to the continuous coefficient sheaves identified in Step 2. On that chart, [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] identifies it with a normalized tower $(N_n)$ of finite free etale sheaves, followed by rationalization. Thus its fibre at $\bar t$ is $(\varprojlim_n(N_n)_{\bar t})\otimes_AE$, the prescription of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves]. The inverse limit is finite free by [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules](1),(2): the reductions have the constant finite free rank near the point. For finitely many maps choose common charts carrying their source and target lattices; the full faithfulness of the rational realization in [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] writes each map as an integral map divided by a power of $arpi$. Changing charts or integral models gives the same fibre maps: the fully faithful rational realization identifies both model maps after restricting to a common chart and clearing their denominators, and the normalized tower maps agree at every level. Hence the construction glues naturally and is independent of these choices. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ extend the resulting $E$-space to $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4),(6); normalized coefficient-system construction of fibres

proof.text: For a short exact sequence in the $E$-heart, take a common connected stratification adapted to its three sheaves using [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification]. Restriction is exact by its clause (3). Refine by common affine etale integral-model charts from [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-affine-etale-lattice], and then by their connected components. Lattice existence for each of the finitely many objects and fibre-product refinement give a common cover; full faithfulness in [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] clears the denominators of the finitely many arrows on each quasi-compact chart. On each such chart the rationalized normalized-system category is the lisse $E$-sheaf category of [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2). The representation equivalence is exact, so evaluating the three representations at a geometric point gives a short exact sequence of finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces. The comparison with the continuous-sheaf category is fully faithful. Include also the lisse kernels and cokernels supplied by [det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure] in the finite list when choosing the model charts. Their universal properties then transport through this fully faithful comparison; they are exactly the corresponding representation kernels and cokernels. Thus the exact sequence being evaluated is precisely the restricted original one. This proves exactness of every fibre functor.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.5 and Lemma 6.8.7, representation calculation on common lisse charts

proof.text: If a heart object has zero fibres everywhere, its continuous-sheaf realization is zero: on any lisse chart the representing $E$-representation has underlying vector space zero, so that local system is zero by [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2) and [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison]. Exact stratum restriction detects zero by [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification](3). For a heart morphism with all fibre maps invertible, exactness from Step 10 makes the fibres of its kernel and cokernel zero. Both are constructible by [det-lem-coefficient-heart-closure], so both vanish, and the morphism is an isomorphism. This proves joint conservativity. Applied to the image of a morphism, the same argument also detects a zero morphism and, by kernels, images and cokernels, detects exactness of short complexes.

source.place: Corollary 6.8.5 and Lemma 6.8.7; zero detection on a finite stratification

proof.text: For $\bar v$ and $\bar t=h\bar v$, restrict to the lisse stratum of $\bar t$ and its fibre-product stratum at $\bar v$. Take an integral-model chart as in Step 9 and base change it along $h$. The comparison [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] identifies module pullback of the lisse model with pullback of its normalized finite etale systems. At each level [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] gives $((h_n)^*N_n)_{\bar v}\cong(N_n)_{\bar t}$, naturally in $N_n$. These maps commute with the quotient transitions, since the stalk comparison is natural. Taking the inverse limit, then tensoring with $E$, gives $(h^*\mathcal F)_{\bar v}\cong\mathcal F_{\bar t}$. The pullback in this calculation is the actual completed rational one by [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization], not an independently chosen heart functor. The local-model independence of Step 9 makes the comparison global and natural.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4 and Remark 6.8.15; finite etale stalk comparison followed by inverse limit and rationalization

proof.text: These constructions commute with finite coefficient extension. On lisse models the comparison [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] is induced by the finite quotient scalar maps. Clause (3) of [lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules] identifies their limits with extension of the finite integral fibre; after inverting the uniformizer this is $F_{\bar t}\otimes_E L$. The tensor and stalk comparison of [lem-pod-lisse-tensor-and-scalar-extension](3) and the transition compatibility in Step 12 ensure that the two routes through a finite extension give the same map on pure tensors, hence the same map. Their identity and composition equations persist. Each finite list of objects, arrows and equations in the common-stage category is represented after a finite enlargement by its definition [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Exactness at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ therefore follows from Step 10 and exactness of vector-space extension; detection follows since extension of fields reflects a nonzero finite-dimensional vector space (a basis remains a basis). This proves the common-stage exactness, conservativity and all scalar-compatibility assertions.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14; normalized finite-stage scalar comparisons and their common-stage descent

proof.text: At each point choose an affine etale chart with an integral model by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-affine-etale-lattice], and identify its normalized local-system model by [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison]. On a connected component of that chart, [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2) identifies its fibres with vector spaces of the one fixed representation, hence with a fixed dimension; every geometric point over a fixed underlying point gives that dimension. The same holds for all choices of algebraically closed field, because the finite etale fibres and their pullback comparisons are [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar]. Since [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map] says etale charts are open, these local ranks descend to a locally constant rank function on each lisse stratum. Thus two geometric fibres over the same point are isomorphic vector spaces, without a claimed canonical choice of isomorphism. Each Noetherian stratum is quasi-compact, so this locally constant function takes finitely many values; refine by its clopen rank loci. The finitely many positive-rank strata form the nonzero-fibre locus, a constructible subset by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ use a common finite coefficient model and Step 13: scalar extension preserves each rank and the zero-rank locus. This proves the final stratification, rank and constructibility clauses.
